cases.name: GET exact body parity and dechunked byte count
HEAD has no body while preserving representation Content-Length
Chunked response streams before completion and preserves exact bytes
Compressed bytes, encoding and known cache metadata remain intact
304 response has zero body and separate status/cache metadata
Concurrent independent GET responses remain correct
Next flags absent/0/1/2/3 forward unchanged while private sentinels never enter logs
Connection-nominated hop headers are stripped both ways; end-to-end header stays
Methods, bodies, targets, Host and field-count violations do not reach upstream
Oversized header is rejected before forwarding without raw-packet logging
Upstream partial-body abort is not reported as a successful full response
Downstream abort is classified with partial observed-body bytes
One real upstream idle timeout returns classified 504 after approximately 30 seconds
CONNECT half-open rejection and bounded owned-process shutdown
Upgrade half-open rejection and bounded owned-process shutdown
CONNECT immediate signal with client write side deliberately left open
Upgrade immediate signal with client write side deliberately left open
Signal during an active ordinary request records interruption and exits without force kill
Duplicate log name refuses without overwriting or appending the original
Invalid port and filename reject before any listener starts
Occupied owned listener refuses without displacing the existing logger
Unavailable fixed upstream produces a classified 502
Logger remains pinned and all logger output remains sentinel-free

notExercised: Concurrency-limit exhaustion and five-thousand-request admission limit
Overlapping slow-stream/backpressure stress; concurrent fast GETs alone do not prove this
Real Next/browser journeys, production transfer savings and cold-tap UX
limitations: Synthetic loopback acceptance, not application, browser, mobile or benchmark evidence
The idle-timeout case is established only if its executed case result says passed; total-deadline/session-expiry checks are outside this suite
Log-write/disk-failure paths and abrupt SIGKILL durability are not certified
Protocol cases inspect EOF and owned-process shutdown; client-side half-open TCP state alone does not prove server handle state
